correction_manifest.title: email_confirm_orig body says 'meeting' in a delivery thread
correction_manifest.current_label: body: 'just to confirm, our meeting is still on for Saturday April 04'
correction_manifest.problem: The email is a reply in the delivery-reschedule thread (thread_id=reschedule_thread). Its subject says 'RE: Delivery for {date}'. But the body says 'our meeting is still on', causing DeepSeek to extract a 'meeting' observation. The transcript_reschedule then extracts a 'delivery' observation. DeepSeek treats them as separate business objects and no contradiction is detected, breaking the P1 scenario intent.
correction_manifest.proposed_fix: Change body to: 'just to confirm, your delivery is still scheduled for Saturday April 04 as originally planned. We haven't made any changes.' Requires corpus regeneration and fingerprint update.
correction_manifest.evidence: signal_id=sig_67d70d5b3e95a57eb6493a19, subject='RE: Delivery for Saturday April 04 — Acme Corp', body contains 'meeting' but not 'delivery'

correction_manifest.title: mtg_02 label includes delivery transcript for a meeting question

correction_manifest.proposed_fix: Remove sig_d992bc383e81974213d7d74a from mtg_02. Updated expected: [meeting_trans, p4_meet_orig, p4_meet_corr]
correction_manifest.evidence: transcript_reschedule body: 'delivery is now rescheduled for Wednesday April 08'

correction_manifest.title: mtg_05 label points to delivery-context signal for meeting question
correction_manifest.problem: Query: 'Find the email confirming a meeting was still happening on the original date for {company}.' email_confirm_orig body currently says 'our meeting is still on' (the CM-01 defect). Once CM-01 is fixed (body → 'delivery'), this signal no longer satisfies the meeting query. A better answer is p4_meeting_orig which is a customer email confirming a meeting on a specific date, without any delivery confusion.
correction_manifest.proposed_fix: Replace email_confirm_orig with p4_meeting_orig (sig_77192f2cc52068f5de5be6b2). p4_meeting_orig body: 'just confirming our meeting is scheduled for {date}. Please add it to your calendar.' — purely a meeting confirmation.
correction_manifest.evidence: p4_meeting_orig subject='Meeting confirmed for Saturday April 04', body contains 'meeting is scheduled' with no delivery mention

correction_manifest.title: voice_qbo is a phantom signal: not generated but referenced in labels
correction_manifest.current_label: voice_qbo=sig_bb6407d8bbe21aaab19720e8 in inv_02, inv_05, inv_10, cross-connector and voice questions
correction_manifest.problem: generator.py never produces a signal with signal_id matching _sig_id(f'voice_qbo_{ent.entity_id}'). The signal is referenced in benchmark_v2.py labels for 5+ question categories per entity (3 entities = 15+ phantom references). inv_05 expected=[dispute_trans, voice_qbo] but only dispute_trans exists (effective denominator=1 not 2). Pass@K scores are unaffected (phantom never retrieved), but set-coverage metrics overcount expected set size.
correction_manifest.proposed_fix: Either: (a) add a voice_qbo signal to generator.py representing a QBO invoice discussion call, OR (b) remove all voice_qbo references from benchmark_v2.py label sets. Option (a) requires corpus regeneration; option (b) is a pure label correction with no corpus change.
correction_manifest.evidence: grep benchmark_v2.py for voice_qbo: 6 references in label sets. grep generator.py for voice_qbo: 0 matches. Verified programmatically in test_p1_semantics.py::TestVoiceQboMissingSignal.
